description:
GOAL: Drive tool usage and reduce friction on scholarship detail pages by surfacing relevant tools contextually — at the exact moment a student is reading eligibility criteria, income limits, or academic cutoffs.

CONTEXT: Right now tools (/tools) and scholarship detail pages (/scholarships/[slug]) are completely siloed. A student reading about a scholarship has to navigate away to use a calculator, which kills momentum.

APPROACH (Phase 1 — Deep Links, ship fast):
Add contextual tool CTAs directly on the detail page at relevant sections:
• Near 'Eligibility Criteria' → Scholarship Eligibility Checker CTA: 'Check if you qualify →'
• Near 'Income Limit' field → Family Income Calculator CTA: 'Verify your household income →'
• Near 'Minimum Marks / CGPA' field → CGPA to Percentage Converter CTA: 'Convert your CGPA →'
• Near 'Benefits / Amount' section → Scholarship Amount Calculator CTA: 'Estimate your benefit →'
• Bottom of page → 'Explore similar tools' strip (passive, links to /tools)

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:
• Start with deep links only (buttons/cards that open the standalone tool page). No inline widgets yet.
• Links can be pre-parameterised if the tool supports URL params (e.g. pre-select category/level based on the scholarship record).
• Use conditional rendering: only show a tool CTA if the relevant DB field is populated (e.g. only show Income Calculator CTA if income_limit field is non-null).
• Target file: app/scholarships/[slug]/page.tsx and relevant subpage components.

PHASE 2 (future, separate ticket): Embed inline mini-widgets on the detail page so students never leave the page.

title: Lead Capture via Scholarship Tools
description:
GOAL: Capture student contact details at the highest-intent moment on the site — immediately after they complete a tool and see their results (e.g. Eligibility Checker shows 5 matching scholarships).

CONTEXT: Parked as of July 2026 until two decisions are made:
1. What do we offer the student in exchange for their contact? (the 'exchange value')
2. What infrastructure will send the follow-up? (email service, WhatsApp API, etc.)

OPTIONS TO DECIDE BETWEEN (for discussion when picking this up):
Option A — 'Email me my results': Zero-friction. Student enters email to receive their eligibility results or tool output. Requires: transactional email service (e.g. Resend, Mailchimp, SendGrid). Easiest to ship.
Option B — 'Get notified when applications open': Student opts in to deadline alerts for matched scholarships. Higher intent, higher value to student. Requires: email service + scheduled job to send alerts when scholarship status changes.
Option C — WhatsApp opt-in: 'Get alerts on WhatsApp'. Higher conversion rate in India. Requires: WhatsApp Business API setup (via Twilio, Interakt, or WATI). More complex setup.

WHERE TO INSERT THE FORM:
• End of Eligibility Checker results (highest intent — student just saw their matches)
• End of CGPA Converter results (after seeing their converted % + matched scholarships)
• End of Family Income Calculator results (after seeing income band + matched schemes)
• Scholarship detail page 'Alert me when this opens' CTA

PRE-REQUISITES BEFORE BUILDING:
• Decide on Option A / B / C above
• Set up chosen email/WhatsApp service and obtain API keys
• Decide on data storage: where leads are stored (a simple DB table, Airtable, Google Sheets, CRM)
• Define the first follow-up sequence (what does the student receive after opt-in?)

NOTE: Do NOT add a generic popup or modal. The opt-in must feel like a natural next step after the tool gives them value.

title: Schema fix: split 'caste' free-text column into caste_tags + eligibility_notes
description:
Context / Why it matters:
The `caste` column does two incompatible jobs at once: it's the field every category filter/pillar-match queries against (via LIKE substring search), AND it stores genuine free-text nuance (e.g. "Brahmin community students under the Brahmin Development Board", Tamil Nadu's Category 1/2A/3A/3B splits, disability sub-criteria). Because nothing enforces a shape at write-time, the column has accumulated at least 5 different formats across ~472 rows: clean JSON arrays, comma-separated strings, JSON arrays of spelled-out community names, and full prose sentences. LIKE-based filtering still works today (substring matches survive any format), but display quality (badges rendering full sentences) and precision logic (isCategoryFocused's "is this scheme category-exclusive" check) are unreliable against the free-text rows. A blind regex-based rewrite risks silently erasing real eligibility nuance (e.g. reducing "Brahmin community students" to ["General"]).

Plan / What to do (in this order, each a separate reviewable step):
1. Add two new columns: `caste_tags` (controlled enum only: SC, ST, OBC, EWS, General, Minority, PWD, EBC, etc. -- no free text ever allowed here) and `eligibility_notes` (free text, for nuance a tag can't capture). Additive migration, does not touch/remove the existing `caste` column, so nothing currently reading `caste` breaks.
2. Auto-populate `caste_tags` for the ~450 rows that are already clean JSON arrays or comma-lists of real category codes -- this is safe and mechanical.
3. Hand-review only the ~15-20 genuinely free-text outliers (the ones found: disability/UDID descriptions, the EWS+Brahmin Development Board scheme, Tamil Nadu's Category 1/2A/3A/3B rows, the various Minority community spellings) and manually assign both caste_tags and eligibility_notes for those.
4. Migrate all category-filtering call sites (getScholarshipsByCategory, isCategoryFocused, getPillarForCategory reverse lookups, category hub pages) to query caste_tags instead of LIKE-matching the raw caste column.
5. Enforce caste_tags as a required, enum-validated field at ingestion time going forward (Antigravity's enrichment pipeline / manual entry / scraping interface -- IS-95), so this doesn't re-accumulate.
6. Only after caste_tags is the source of truth everywhere, consider deprecating/removing the raw `caste` column -- separate, later decision.

Explicitly NOT in scope: a one-shot automated rewrite of the existing `caste` column. That was correctly rejected as too risky given the free-text outliers.

title: Implement simplified Detail page template (content-first redesign + lead-gen-first CTA hierarchy)
description:
Context / Why it matters:
Worked out with Claude via HTML mockups, refined after reviewing Buddy4Study's detail-page CTA pattern. Current ScholarshipDetailTemplate.tsx (app/components/ScholarshipDetailTemplate.tsx) is visually noisy — colored section bars, gradient CTA card, Telegram promo card, trust badge card, and a card-grid 'Similar Scholarships' section all compete with the Apply CTA. Beyond decluttering, the CTA *hierarchy* itself is changing: this is the site's most-visited page (PM Yashasvi), so what sits above the fold matters most here. Decision: the outbound 'Apply on official portal' link is NOT gated (we still link out, unlike Buddy4Study's signup wall) but is deliberately moved OUT of the hero — it now lives in its own section next to 'How to Apply', contextually placed where someone reading the steps needs it, not as the first thing shown. The top-of-fold primary CTA slot instead goes to lead-gen (Follow this scholarship / Get deadline alerts), which also becomes the only CTA that persists as a sticky bar while scrolling — the outbound Apply link does not get a sticky treatment, to avoid re-introducing the same attention competition we removed.

Plan / What to do:
Rebuild ScholarshipDetailTemplate.tsx following the agreed mock: eyebrow + breadcrumb for orientation, 3 plain facts (amount/deadline/status), a lead-gen CTA row above the fold (Follow / Get Alerts) as the single loud accent-colored element up top, spec-list eligibility (not card grid), numbered How-to-Apply steps with the outbound portal link embedded directly in that section (not the hero), native <details> FAQ, then the 4-group related-content section in priority order: Pillar/guide (evergreen, bold) -> related how-to -> other scholarships across ALL matching facets (state/category/level — see IS-116) -> related news. Preserve every existing data field with zero omissions (this is the most-visited page — verified against live DB row: amount tiers by class, income limit, age limit, special_conditions, total_awards=30000, renewal policy, helpline, verification/last_verified line, full FAQ set, selection criteria, documents, step_guide). Lead-gen CTA copy/backend depends on IS-76 decision (email first).

Trigger:
Design agreed in conversation, mock reviewed and iterated; CTA hierarchy changed per direct feedback: 'I don't want the CTA linking out to be above the fold... move it to its own section like B4S and don't surface it above the fold' — lead-gen CTAs (Follow/Alerts) take the prime real estate instead.

Resolution:
Discovered ScholarshipDetailTemplate.tsx (the component originally mocked against) was actually dead code — the real live page is the 1249-line app/scholarships/[slug]/page.tsx itself. Rewrote it in full: preserved 100% of the SEO logic (all per-slug title overrides, metadata, hreflang, OG tags), all data fetching, all 3 JSON-LD schemas (Article/FAQ/GovernmentService), and the FormattedText parser exactly as-is. Replaced only the visual layer: removed the dark gradient hero, the repeated sidebar CTA card, all colored 'Direct Answer' blockquotes (blue/emerald/red/gray), the 3-column sticky-sidebar grid layout, and the colored pillar/sibling-variant callout boxes. New structure: plain eyebrow+title, 3-fact strip (amount/deadline/status), real ShareButtons as the only above-fold action (no fake Follow/Alerts buttons — those need IS-76 lead-capture decided and built first, so the honest choice was to keep Apply as the real primary action rather than fake a feature that doesn't exist), a dedicated 'Ready to apply?' section with the real outbound link placed contextually near How-to-Apply, plain spec-list eligibility, numbered how-to-apply steps, plain-list Discover More (moved out of the sidebar into the single-column flow), and every related-content section (news, guides, similar scholarships) as plain lists.

Verified locally on PM Yasasvi (highest-traffic page): every single field confirmed present with zero loss — sibling variants, best-fit pillar, benefits, special conditions, eligibility, selection, renewal, all 7 apply steps, documents, deadline, quick facts (total awards), all 3 FAQs, helpline, discover-more links, disclaimer, 5 related news items, 2 related guides, 3 similar scholarships. Zero console errors. Confirmed no regression on a scholarship with fewer optional fields (Bihar Post-Matric). npx tsc --noEmit clean across the whole project.

Changes: removed the gradient hero background and solid-filled colored badge, replaced with the mock's plain bordered content-type tag; 'Key Takeaways' box de-tinted from indigo-filled to a plain top/bottom-border block; 'Jump to a Hub' card grid converted to a plain bordered list; 'Related Step-by-Step Guides' and 'Latest News' card grids (gray/red-tinted boxes) converted to the same plain-list pattern. Consolidated the accent color: this section previously used a separate 'indigo' accent distinct from the rest of the site's 'google-blue' brand color — replaced every indigo instance (component files AND the markdown-to-HTML renderer in lib/pillars.ts, which was hardcoding indigo into rendered links/code/blockquotes/auto-linked scholarship mentions) with google-blue, so Editorial content now genuinely shares one accent with the rest of the site, not two.

The News template (IS-114) is also still separate/untouched.

Proof of concept shipped:
Built lib/editorial.ts — a unified EditorialContent TypeScript schema (superset of Pillar/Article/PortalGuide, every field mapped, none lost — includes the key distinction between static `schemes` lists and live `relatedScholarshipQuery` DB lookups, and grouped `steps` to support Portal Guides' separate login-steps vs status-steps sequences). Built app/components/EditorialTemplate.tsx — a single generic renderer with conditional blocks (content tag, key facts strip, takeaways, hub links, official-portal link, TOC, checklist, grouped numbered steps, schemes list, FAQ accordion, helpline) that only render when the corresponding schema field is present. Wrote portalGuideToEditorial() adapter and wired app/guides/[portal]/page.tsx so the ssp-karnataka portal (proof case) now renders entirely through the new unified template instead of its old bespoke JSX — every other portal still uses the legacy template until verified further.

Verified locally: /guides/ssp-karnataka renders correctly through the new template — key facts, checklist, BOTH step groups (Student Login & Registration + Checking Application Status, correctly split from loginSteps/statusSteps), top schemes, FAQ accordion, and helpline all confirmed present with zero console errors. Confirmed no regression: other portals (Digital Gujarat) still render via the legacy template unaffected; Pillars (Karnataka) still render correctly via their own delegation path.

This proves the schema/renderer genuinely handles a Portal Guide's structure (the most different of the three types — the only one with grouped steps + static schemes + helpline), not just Pillars. Remaining work to fully close this ticket: migrate the other 7 portals onto the same adapter/template (mechanical once ssp-karnataka is proven), then do the equivalent for Articles (needs an articleToEditorial adapter + retiring InteractiveArticleBody), then decide whether Pillars should also route through EditorialTemplate directly rather than their own still-separate (though now visually-matching) PillarBody component.

Full migration completed:
1) All 8 Portal Guides now render through EditorialTemplate via portalGuideToEditorial() — removed ~380 lines of dead legacy JSX from app/guides/[portal]/page.tsx, cleaned up now-unused imports (PORTAL_NAV_ITEMS, several lucide icons, slugify, Link). HowTo + FAQ JSON-LD schema preserved. Verified all 7 non-NSP portals render correctly, zero console errors, zero regression. NSP is separately blocked by the pre-existing IS-120 bug (unrelated).
2) Built articleToEditorial() adapter (lib/editorial.ts) — maps ArticleData's featuredStats, takeaways, checklist, faqs, relatedScholarships, targetMoneyLink into the schema. Added two new schema fields discovered as genuinely needed during this pass: featuredScholarships (pre-resolved render list — the DB fetch for relatedScholarshipSlugs/relatedScholarshipQuery happens at the page level, template just renders the result) and relatedGuides restructured to take pre-resolved {title, href, meta} objects instead of raw slugs, both following the same 'resolve at the page, render generically' convention already established. Rewrote app/articles/[slug]/page.tsx (288 lines -> ~145) to use EditorialTemplate, keeping the two genuinely one-off special cases (stats-report featured image, UP Status Decoder widget) as small page-level extras around the shared template rather than forcing them into the generic schema. Verified locally: a plain article (Bihar PMS) renders fully with TOC/takeaways/checklist/FAQ; the stats-report special case shows its banner image; the UP-decoder special case shows its widget; a rich article (SC/ST Freeship Card) correctly resolves and displays its 'Featured Scholarships' block with real DB data matching frontmatter exactly. Zero console errors across all cases.

app/components/InteractiveArticleBody.tsx is now dead code (zero remaining imports anywhere) — left in place rather than deleted, in case any in-flight content still references it; safe to remove in a follow-up cleanup pass.

Ticket closed. All three original systems (Pillars, Articles, Portal Guides) now render through one shared EditorialTemplate + one shared schema. News (IS-114) remains intentionally separate.

title: Implement simplified News page template
description:

title: Consolidate Guides + Articles + Pillars into one /guides Editorial namespace (routing/redirects)
description:
Context / Why it matters:
Taxonomy decision made in conversation with Claude: /guides (app/guides/[portal]) and /articles (content/articles/*) are the same underlying content type — narrow, step-by-step portal walkthroughs — built twice in two different route trees with two different templates. Pillars (content/pillars/*) are structurally different (broad, evergreen topic guides) and should remain distinguishable, but all three should share one Editorial identity instead of three inconsistently-labeled sections (all three currently self-describe as 'Scholarship Guides' in their page titles, which is the root cause of the original 'no cohesion' complaint that started this whole discussion).

Plan / What to do:
This is an SEO-sensitive migration, not a simple rename — requires a full 301 redirect map before any URL changes ship. Steps: 1) Audit all live Guide/Article/Pillar URLs and their current search performance. 2) Decide final URL structure (e.g. keep /guides for how-to depth, /pillars for evergreen depth, drop /articles entirely or fold into /guides). 3) Build redirect map. 4) Migrate content into the unified Editorial template (IS-{next_id+2}). 5) Update Header.tsx nav and Footer.tsx to reflect the collapsed taxonomy (currently lists Guides, Articles, Pillars as 3 separate top-level items). 6) Monitor Search Console post-migration.

Trigger:
Taxonomy decision made in conversation — do NOT execute URL changes without the redirect plan step above.

Progress:
Phase 1 shipped: added 301 redirects in next.config.ts for the 4 confirmed duplicate articles (identified in CNT-52) to their matching live Portal Guide — /articles/digital-gujarat-scholarship-portal-guide -> /guides/digital-gujarat-mysy, /articles/karnataka-ssp-postmatric-guide-2026 -> /guides/ssp-karnataka, /articles/mp-taas-scholarship-portal-guide -> /guides/mptaas-mmvy-mp, /articles/how-to-apply-talliki-vandanam-eligibility-status -> /guides/talliki-vandanam-ap. Verified locally: all 4 redirect correctly; confirmed no regression on an unrelated unique article (bihar-postmatric-pms-guide). 5 Pillar files still reference the old article slugs in relatedArticleSlugs frontmatter — redirect keeps those links working (one extra hop), optional polish to update directly, not required for correctness.

Phase 2 NOT started (blocked on IS-113): the other 24 unique articles have no destination yet — migrating them requires the unified Editorial template landing first, then expanding portalsData.ts (or equivalent) with new entries, then redirecting old -> new. Also still open: what to do with the 1 stats-report article, and the eventual Header/Footer nav taxonomy update once migration is complete.

Decision revised in conversation: rather than 'Pillars stay separate at /pillars, only Articles absorb into /guides', the user opted to absorb ALL THREE into one /guides URL namespace now, while Pillars are still new/low-traffic — cheaper to move now than after they accumulate rankings. Classification (Pillar vs How-To vs News) becomes a taxonomy/metadata concern, not a URL concern — relevant given a headless WordPress migration is being considered, where this is the natural post-type+taxonomy model anyway.

Phase 1c shipped: app/guides/[portal]/page.tsx now delegates to the existing Pillar page component (app/pillars/[slug]/page.tsx, reused as-is, not duplicated) whenever the requested slug isn't a known portal id/alias but IS a Pillar slug. generateStaticParams and generateMetadata both updated to cover Pillar slugs, with metadata's canonical correctly pointing at /guides/... not /pillars/.... Added one parameterized redirect in next.config.ts (/pillars/:slug -> /guides/:slug) covering all 25 Pillars, since destination slug always equals source slug — no need to hardcode 25 entries. The /pillars index page itself is untouched (redirect only matches individual pillar pages).

Verified locally: /guides/karnataka-scholarships-guide renders full pillar content (takeaways, hub links, TOC) correctly; /pillars/karnataka-scholarships-guide redirects there; /guides/sc-st-scholarships-india-guide works; existing portal guides (ssp-karnataka, digital-gujarat-mysy) unaffected — no regression. /pillars index page still renders normally.

Known follow-up, not yet done: internal cross-links (Pillar hubLinks/relatedPillarSlug frontmatter, and the Header mega-menu's 'All Scholarship Guides' link) still point at old /pillars/... URLs — these still work via the redirect (one extra hop) but should eventually be updated to link directly at /guides/... Also: the /pillars and /guides INDEX pages are still two separate pages (one lists only Pillars, one lists only Portal Guides) — merging those into one combined index is separate follow-up work, not done here.

Still fully blocked on IS-113: the 24 unique Articles (from CNT-52's audit) still have no destination — they need the unified Editorial template before they can move into /guides too.

Phase 2 completed:
The remaining 24 unique Articles now also render under /guides/[slug], via the same delegation pattern proven on Pillars — app/guides/[portal]/page.tsx now checks portal -> Pillar -> Article in order before returning notFound(). generateStaticParams and generateMetadata both cover Article slugs (metadata built inline with a /guides/... canonical, not delegated to the Article page's own generateMetadata which still points at /articles/...). Added a generic redirect '/articles/:slug' -> '/guides/:slug' in next.config.ts, placed AFTER the 4 explicit article-to-different-slug overrides so those still win (verified: /articles/karnataka-ssp-postmatric-guide-2026 still correctly redirects to /guides/ssp-karnataka, not to a same-named guides route). Also fixed the Article page's internal cross-links (sibling 'More on This Topic' links, breadcrumb label) to point directly at /guides instead of /articles, removing the redirect hop on-site.

Verified locally: /guides/bihar-postmatric-pms-guide renders correctly at the direct URL; /articles/bihar-postmatric-pms-guide redirects there; the 4 explicit overrides still take priority over the new generic rule; breadcrumb correctly reads 'Guides' not 'Articles'; Pillars and Portal Guides both confirmed unaffected. npx tsc --noEmit clean, zero console errors.

Ticket fully closed. Every Pillar, Portal Guide, and Article now lives under one /guides URL namespace, per the original decision — 'am not a software dev, I want everything absorbed into one /guides.'

Phase 3 (index-page collapse): user flagged that /pillars was still live and linked from the homepage despite individual pillar pages redirecting, then explicitly directed 'the index pages of /pillar /articles need to be collapsed into /guides.' Rewrote app/guides/page.tsx to merge all three former index pages into one: Pillar sections (by classification: topic/category/course/provider/state guides, logic reused verbatim from the old app/pillars/page.tsx), a 'State & Central Portal Guides' grid (the 8 hardcoded Portal entries + 2 utility guides), and a new 'How-To Guides' grid of Articles (via getAllArticles(), filtering out the 4 slugs that already have an explicit Portal-guide redirect override so they aren't listed twice). Deleted app/pillars/page.tsx and app/articles/page.tsx outright (fully superseded). Added two new next.config.ts redirects: '/pillars' -> '/guides' and '/articles' -> '/guides' (index-level, permanent). Updated internal nav: Header.tsx (removed the redundant top-level 'Articles' link, fixed 4 internal /pillars and /articles references to /guides, updated one mobile-menu label from 'Help Articles' to 'Step-by-Step Help Guides'), Footer.tsx (collapsed 3 separate Resources links — Scholarship Guides / How to Apply Guides / Help Articles — into one 'Scholarship Guides' link to /guides), HomeClient.tsx (de-indigo'd the Scholarship Guides homepage section to google-blue, fixed 3 links from /pillars or /articles to /guides). Confirmed app/components/ScholarshipDetailTemplate.tsx is genuine dead code (zero imports anywhere in app/) so its stray /articles reference was deliberately left as-is.

Verified locally: npx tsc --noEmit clean. Dev server console showed zero errors. /guides index confirmed rendering all sections — Pillar classification sections, 'State & Central Portal Guides' (16+ portal cards incl. Karnataka/Gujarat/Jharkhand/Kerala), and 'How-To Guides'. /pillars and /articles (bare index URLs) both confirmed live-redirecting to /guides via window.location.href checks. Individual /guides/[slug] delegation spot-checked still working post-change (e.g. /guides/minority-scholarships-guide renders full Pillar content correctly, zero console errors). Noted in passing: /guides/nsp 404s due to a pre-existing, unrelated redirect bug (already logged as IS-120 — a stale '-nsp' suffixed destination slug that doesn't exist) — not caused by or fixed in this batch.

Not yet committed/pushed as of this note — pending user go-ahead, consistent with this session's pattern of only pushing on explicit request.

title: Cross-link scholarships across hub types (State/Category/Level/Income) for findability
description:
Context / Why it matters:
Core outcome of the taxonomy/findability discussion with Claude. Confirmed via DB counts and a Buddy4Study comparison that a faceted model (State, Category, Level, Income, Provider-type, Course, University as independent, co-equal facets) is correct for this dataset — NOT a single 'primary' hierarchy (47% of scholarships are 'All India' with no state, and SC/ST/OBC/General are near-universal so they don't discriminate well as a tree). The gap isn't the number of hubs, it's that a scholarship belonging to multiple facets simultaneously (e.g. a Karnataka + SC/ST + UG scholarship) currently only surfaces sibling links for whichever ONE hub the visiting page happens to be on — there's no cross-awareness between facet types.

Plan / What to do:
Extend the Detail page's related-scholarships module (already redesigned per IS-111) to pull siblings from ALL of the current scholarship's facets, not just one — e.g. 'Other scholarships in Karnataka' + 'Other SC/ST scholarships' + 'Other Undergraduate scholarships', each as its own short plain-list group. Mirrors getRelatedScholarships() in lib/db.ts but needs to surface multiple facet groups instead of one blended ranked list.

Trigger:
Taxonomy/findability discussion with Claude — confirmed this matters more than picking a 'primary' category.

title: Add persistent site-wide taxonomy block (footer, all pages) — Buddy4Study-style
description:
Context / Why it matters:
Found via direct comparison with Buddy4Study (1,706+ scholarships vs. our 476). Their entire findability strategy for hub pages isn't breadcrumbs or hierarchy — it's one taxonomy block (State-wise / Class-based / Type-based, 8 links each = 24 total) repeated in the footer on every single page, site-wide. We currently bury most of this one click deep in the mega-menu, and it doesn't appear at all on Detail, Editorial, or News pages.

Plan / What to do:
Add a persistent 3-column taxonomy block to Footer.tsx (or a new shared component rendered on every page type): State hubs, Category/Type hubs, Education-level hubs, mirroring the coverage audit done in conversation (we already match or exceed Buddy4Study on State/Category/Government/Course — this just needs to be visible everywhere, not just the mega-menu). Include the currently-orphaned Course and International hubs (IS-106, IS-107) once those land.

Trigger:
Buddy4Study competitive comparison in conversation with Claude.

title: Make breadcrumbs referrer-aware instead of a fixed fake hierarchy
description:
Context / Why it matters:
Discussed with Claude: since a scholarship genuinely has multiple valid parents (its state, its category, its level, its income bracket — all independent, none more 'true' than another), a single fixed breadcrumb pretends one facet is canonical when it isn't. Confirmed breadcrumbs matter on both desktop and mobile (mobile especially for Google's BreadcrumbList rich-snippet rendering in mobile search results), so this isn't about removing them — it's about which parent they show.

Plan / What to do:
Have the breadcrumb default to whichever facet the visitor actually arrived through (read from referrer/query param when available — e.g. arriving from a state hub shows State in the breadcrumb, arriving from a category hub shows Category), falling back to a sensible default (state if present, else category) when no referrer signal exists. Keep BreadcrumbList JSON-LD schema present on every page regardless of visual display.

Trigger:
Taxonomy/findability discussion with Claude.

title: Prune or merge near-zero-value hub pages (thin facet combinations)
description:
Context / Why it matters:
Found via DB count audit in conversation. Several hub combinations have 0-2 active scholarships (e.g. PWD category pre-cleanup, several single-scholarship states/UTs like Lakshadweep, Nagaland, Puducherry). Buddy4Study handles this by backfilling thin facet pages with a generic 'Featured Scholarships' carousel rather than showing a near-empty page — worth adopting the same pattern rather than either hiding these pages or leaving them looking broken.

Plan / What to do:
Audit all generated hub pages for scholarship count. For any hub under ~3 results, either (a) blend in a 'More scholarships you may be eligible for' fallback module (same general-listing pattern Buddy4Study uses), or (b) redirect/merge into a parent hub with a pre-applied filter instead of a standalone thin page. Decide threshold and fallback design.

Trigger:
DB count audit + Buddy4Study comparison in conversation with Claude.

title: BUG (pre-existing): /guides/nsp redirects to a dead slug and 404s
description:
Context / Why it matters:
Found while verifying IS-115's Pillar-to-/guides routing change (unrelated to that change — this bug already existed in next.config.ts before today). The redirect `/guides/nsp/:subpage*` -> `/guides/national-scholarship-portal-nsp/:subpage*` uses a `:subpage*` wildcard (zero-or-more), so it also matches the bare /guides/nsp URL with no subpage — but the destination slug 'national-scholarship-portal-nsp' doesn't exist anywhere in portalsData.ts. The real NSP portal's id is 'nsp' with aliases ['national-scholarship-portal', 'scholarships-gov-in'] — no '-nsp' suffix variant. Result: /guides/nsp currently 404s in production.

Plan / What to do:
Fix the redirect destination to point at a real slug (likely just remove this redirect entirely, since 'nsp' is already the canonical id and doesn't need rewriting to a longer alias) — or if the intent was legacy-URL support, correct the destination to 'national-scholarship-portal' (matching the real alias) instead of 'national-scholarship-portal-nsp'.

Trigger:
Found during IS-115 verification. Live bug, affects a page for the site's flagship central portal.

title: BUG: Mobile menu missing Course/Income/Study Abroad/Sports/PWD links (desktop-only fix)
description:

title: Header: restructure for orientation — mega-menu still doesn't expose all real categories, feels cluttered
description:
Context / Why it matters:
User feedback: 'header continues to have cluttered navigation without orientation.' Confirmed gap — even after this session's additions, the mega-menu mixes hub links, curated collections (Trending/Deadlines/New Arrivals), and provider-type links in a flat 3-column layout with no visual hierarchy signaling which items are peer categories vs. one-off collections. It also still doesn't expose every real category (Income limit hubs missing from Popular Segments column, for example).

Plan / What to do:
Full redesign pass on the mega-menu structure, not just adding missing links. Needs a clear grouping principle (e.g. 'Browse by facet' vs 'Curated views' vs 'Learn') so a user can tell at a glance what kind of thing each link is, per the taxonomy work already done in IS-116/117. Should resolve alongside IS-123 (trending/deadlines nav consolidation) since they're the same underlying problem — collections presented as peers of categories.

User feedback with mobile-menu screenshot, this session.

title: Footer: still incomplete — needs the full persistent taxonomy block (supersedes/absorbs IS-117)
description:

This session only added 4 links to the existing 'Browse' list (Course, Study Abroad, Sports, PWD) — the bigger IS-117 redesign (full 3-column Buddy4Study-style taxonomy block, visible on every page) was never done. Confirmed still missing from footer entirely: Income hubs.

User feedback, this session — confirms IS-117 is still the right call and now has direct user confirmation, not just competitive research.

title: Nav: present Trending/Deadlines/Recently-Added as views within Browse, not peer top-level items
description:
Context / Why it matters:
User asked whether /scholarships, /scholarships/trending, and /scholarships/deadlines should be collapsed. Checked first: they are NOT duplicates — each has distinct, real SEO metadata targeting different search intent ('trending scholarships' vs 'scholarship deadlines 2026' vs generic), and /scholarships/deadlines is a substantial 450-line feature page (countdown timers, filters), not a thin wrapper. Merging the URLs would destroy real ranking pages — same mistake class as the Article duplicates, but the opposite conclusion.

Plan / What to do:
The problem is navigational presentation, not routing. Currently the mobile 'Quick Actions Grid' and desktop mega-menu present Trending/Deadlines/New Arrivals/All Schemes as 4 equal-weight, disconnected buttons. Restructure so these read as sort/filter views of one 'Browse Scholarships' destination (e.g. one primary Browse entry point, with Trending/Deadlines/Recently-Added shown as a secondary row or toggle within it), not as separate peer destinations. Keep all URLs unchanged — this is a presentation-only fix.

User feedback, this session — direct question about collapsing these routes.

title: Homepage: doesn't lead users into underrepresented categories or Editorial/News content
description:
Context / Why it matters:
User feedback: 'Homepage needs to lead people into unrepresented pages and categories as well as editorial and news content.' Current homepage has a 'Category Gateway' section (By State Domicile, By Social Category grids) but it's unclear whether it covers Course/Income/Sports/PWD/Study Abroad, or surfaces Editorial (Pillars/Guides) or News at all — needs an audit against what's actually there versus what's missing, then a fix.

Plan / What to do:
Audit HomeClient.tsx against the full real taxonomy (State, Category, Education Level, Income, Course, University, Provider type, Study Abroad, Sports, PWD) and against Editorial/News — list what's exposed vs. missing, then add dedicated sections for whatever's absent, prioritizing categories with real scholarship counts that currently have zero homepage presence.

User feedback, this session.

title: BUG: International scholarships leaking into Trending/Deadlines/Recently Added
description:
Context / Why it matters:
User noticed /scholarships/trending and /scholarships/deadlines showing Study Abroad scholarships (ESMT Berlin MBA, University of Calgary, ADB-Japan, DAAD, Hubert Humphrey Fellowship) mixed in with domestic ones, undifferentiated. Root cause: two separate, parallel implementations exist. getTrendingScholarships()/getClosingSoonScholarships() in lib/db.ts (used by the homepage carousels) had no scholarship_scope filter. Separately, and more impactfully, ScholarshipsList.tsx (the shared component actually powering the live /scholarships/trending and /scholarships/deadlines PAGES via getAllScholarships() + client-side filter/sort) also had zero scope awareness — confirmed several International scholarships share the same top priority_score (95/90) as the best domestic ones, so they were winning the sort and appearing as the featured highlight.

Resolution:
Added a scope exclusion to both: the two lib/db.ts query functions (SQL-level 'AND (LOWER(scholarship_scope) IS NOT 'international')'), and ScholarshipsList.tsx's client-side filter (excludes any row with scholarship_scope='international' unconditionally, since this shared component has no International tab/mode at all — that content type only lives at /scholarships/international with its own dedicated hub and query functions).

Verified locally: /scholarships/trending dropped from 372 to 269 results with ESMT Berlin/Calgary/ADB-Japan/DAAD all gone from the top of the list; /scholarships/deadlines confirmed clean (3 results, all domestic). npx tsc --noEmit clean. Zero console errors.

Trigger:
User feedback, this session — flagged as a real, confusing UX issue, not a hypothetical.

title: Collapse /guides/[portal]/[subpage] into single portal pages — retire per-portal subpage generation
description:
Context / Why it matters:
The /guides/[portal]/[subpage] route (app/guides/[portal]/[subpage]/page.tsx) statically generates 4-5 thin subpages per portal (status-check, student-login, documents-list, scholarships-list, schemes alias) across all 9 portals in lib/portalsData.ts — roughly 45 low-content URLs, each just a template wrapper around portal metadata with little unique substance per subpage.

Now that we have a unified editorial articles section (content/articles/*.md, rendered at /articles/[slug]) covering the same ground with real, substantive content — NSP status checks, PFMS tracking, documents guides, etc. are already covered there — we don't want thin, templated portal subpages competing with or diluting that content.

Plan / What to do:
1. Collapse each portal's subpages back onto a single /guides/[portal] overview page (app/guides/[portal]/page.tsx already exists for this) — fold the status-check / student-login / documents-list / scholarships-list content into sections or tabs on that one page instead of separate URLs.
2. Remove the generateStaticParams portal x subpage matrix and the PORTAL_SUBPAGES page generation logic in app/guides/[portal]/[subpage]/page.tsx.
3. Add 301 redirects from the old /guides/[portal]/[subpage] URLs to the consolidated /guides/[portal] page (or to the relevant /articles/[slug] piece where one now exists, e.g. /guides/pfms/status-check -> /articles/pfms-scholarship-payment-status-tracking-guide) to preserve any existing SEO equity.
4. Audit content/articles and internal links (several new articles link to /guides/nsp/status-check, /guides/mahadbt/documents-list, etc.) and repoint them to the surviving consolidated URLs.

Trigger:
User decision, 2026-07-29: now that editorial articles exist as the substantive content layer, stop generating thin per-portal subpages — collapse to one page per portal and remove the subpage-generation rule.
